outputs.exact_statement: There are infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p-1$ is squarefree and $\Omega(p-1)$ is even. In particular, there are infinitely many such primes under either convention for counting prime factors.

Let $f$ be real-valued on an interval containing $H$ consecutive integers. If $f'$ is monotone and remains in $[j+\lambda,j+1-\lambda]$ for an integer $j$ and $0<\lambda\le1/2$, then $$\sum_n\mathrm{e}(f(n))\ll\lambda^{-1}.$$ If instead $f$ is twice continuously differentiable and $\lambda\le|f''|\le C\lambda$ throughout the interval, then $$\sum_n\mathrm{e}(f(n))\ll_C H\sqrt\lambda+\lambda^{-1/2}.$$ Both estimates apply on every subinterval satisfying their hypotheses.

Let $F$ be smooth and supported on a fixed bounded box in $\mathbb{R}^b$, with $b$ fixed. Suppose all derivatives of order $j$ are bounded by $C_jL^{C(j+1)}$. Fourier inversion separates its variables with integrated absolute coefficient mass $L^{O(1)}$. There is a fixed exponent $C'>0$, depending on $b,C$, such that truncating each frequency at $L^{C'}$ makes an error $O_A(L^{-A})$ for every fixed $A>0$. The exponent $C'$ is fixed before $A$.

Fix $0<\tau<\eta<1$, $C>0$, and $A>0$. There is a constant $B_0=B_0(\tau,\eta,C,A)$ such that, uniformly for $$\frac{x^\tau}{2}\le N\le x^\eta,\qquad
 q\le L^C,\qquad L^{B_0}\le |t|\le x^2,$$ every Dirichlet character $\chi$ modulo $q$ and every interval $I\subset[N,2N]$ satisfy $$\label{lp:prime-estimate}
 \left|\sum_{p\in I}\chi(p)p^{-1+it}\right|
 \ll_{\tau,\eta,C,A} L^{-A}.$$

Fix $C>0$. There is an absolute constant $C_3>0$ such that, for sufficiently large $x$ in terms of $C$, the following holds uniformly: $$\exp(L/T^2)\le N'\le2x^5,\qquad q\le L^C,\qquad
 \exp(L/(2T^2))\le |v|\le4x^3.$$ For every residue $a\pmod q$ and every interval $I\subset[N',2N']$, $$\label{lp:progression-estimate}
 \left|\sum_{\substack{n\in I\\n\equiv a\pmod q}}n^{iv}\right|
 \ll \frac{N'}q\exp(-L/T^{C_3}).$$

Fix $C>0$ and put $r_*=T^4/L$. Uniformly for $q\le L^C$, $$\label{lp:L-upper-bound}
 \log|D(\sigma+iv,\chi)|\ll_C T^2
 \quad\left(|\sigma-1|\le10r_*,\quad
                   \frac12\le|v|\le3x^3\right).$$

There is a fixed $C$ such that, for each fixed $\sigma>0$, $$\sum_{\substack{r>x^\sigma\\r_*=1}}\frac{W_1(r)}r
 \le L^C\exp(-\sigma L^{3/5})$$ for all sufficiently large $x$.

There is a fixed $C_A$ such that $$X_A\asymp\frac{x}{L}H_QH_P,
 \qquad X_A\gg xL^{-C_A}.$$ The implied constants and $C_A$ depend only on the fixed geometry and on $\Psi$.

The mass of nonsquarefree predecessors satisfies $$\sum_{\substack{u\ge1\\2u\ {\rm not\ squarefree}}}
       A(u)\Psi(u/x)=o(X_A/L).$$

For every fixed $0<\vartheta<1/2$ and $D>0$, $$\sum_{\substack{d\le x^\vartheta\\d\ {\rm odd\ and\ squarefree}}}
       |r(d)|\ll_{\vartheta,D}xL^{-D}+X_A L^{-18}.$$ The constants may depend on the fixed weight geometry and $\Psi$, but not on any later proxy precision. No effective bound on the threshold for $x$ is asserted.

An assignment $a$ consists of the complete ordered $r_0$-tuples in all the micro bands and one prime mark from each $\mathcal P_g$. Let $D_1=D_1(a)$ be their product, with multiplicities retained, and put $$\lambda_a=\prod_{j=j'}^{j_x}\frac1{r_0!}\prod_g V_g^{-1}.$$ For sufficiently large $x$, $$\label{ex:assignment-masses} D_1\le x^{1/20},\qquad \sum_a\frac{\lambda_a}{D_1}\ll H_Q,\qquad \sum_a\lambda_a\ll x^{1/20}H_Q.$$ For each assignment, ban every odd non-$\mathcal P$ prime at most $x^\theta$ not dividing $D_1$, and independently ban each $\mathcal P$ prime not dividing $D_1$ with probability $1-q_0$. With expectation over this finite random mask, $$\label{ex:positive-majorant} A(u)\le A_0(u)\le \sum_a\lambda_a\mathbf{1}_{D_1\mid u}\,\mathbb E_a \mathbf{1}_{u\text{ is divisible by no banned prime}}.$$ The constants in [ex:assignment-masses] depend only on the fixed weight geometry and $j'$.

In all factor sums used below, a test $I$ on either factor of $mn=N_u$ can be replaced by $B_I$ with total error $o(X_A/L)$, provided the coefficient on the other factor has absolute value at most one. This holds also when that other coefficient is a proxy.

The weight of prime values $N_u$, together with composite values whose least prime factor exceeds $x^{1/2-\kappa}$, is at least $$\label{ex:surviving-mass}
 \frac{\mathfrak S X_A}{2L}$$ for sufficiently large $x$ after $b_1$ is chosen sufficiently small.

With the constant fixed in [ex:balanced-constant], the weight of composite $N_u$ with $P^-(N_u)>x^{1/2-\kappa}$ is at most $$\label{ex:balanced-bound} C_{\mathrm{bal}}(\kappa+1/L)\frac{X_A}{L}+o(X_A/L).$$
